1.name: Spellcasting
1.notes:
You learn to channel the magic of nature to cast Ranger spells.

Spell Slots. The Ranger Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Ranger spells of level 1+ that you can cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 spells (Cure Wounds and Ensnaring Strike are recommended). Your number of prepared spells increases as you gain Ranger levels, as shown in the class table. Prepared spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
If another Ranger feature grants you spells that are always prepared, they don’t count against your number of prepared spells.

Changing Prepared Spells. When you finish a Long Rest, you may replace one prepared spell with another Ranger spell you can cast.

Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Ranger spells.

1.name: Favored Enemy
1.notes:
You always have the Hunter’s Mark spell prepared. You can cast it twice without expending a spell slot, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
You gain additional free uses of Hunter’s Mark at higher levels, as shown in the class table.

1.name: Weapon Mastery
1.notes:
You can use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency.
Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you may change the weapon types whose mastery properties you can use (for example, switching from Longbows and Shortswords to Scimitars and Longswords).

2.name: Deft Explorer
2.notes:
Your journeys have strengthened your survival skills.

Expertise. Choose one of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise; you gain Expertise in that skill.

Languages. You learn two additional languages of your choice from the standard language lists.

2.name: Fighting Style
2.notes:
You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice.

Alternatively, you may choose Druidic Warrior: you learn two Druid cantrips (Guidance and Starry Wisp are recommended). These cantrips count as Ranger spells for you, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a Ranger level, you may replace one of these cantrips with another Druid cantrip.

3.name: Dreadful Strikes
3.notes: You can infuse your weapon attacks with Feywild magic. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you may deal an extra 1d4 Psychic damage. A creature can take this extra damage only once per turn. This extra damage increases to 1d6 at Ranger level 11.

3.name: Fey Wanderer Spells
3.notes:
You always have the following spells prepared at the listed Ranger levels:

3rd: Charm Person
5th: Misty Step
9th: Summon Fey
13th: Dimension Door
17th: Mislead

You also gain a Feywild Gift (roll or choose):
1. Illusory butterflies appear during rests.
2. Flowers bloom from your hair each dawn.
3. You smell faintly of a comforting herb or spice.
4. Your shadow moves independently when not observed.
5. Horns or antlers grow from your head.
6. Your skin and hair shift color each dawn.

3.name: Otherworldly Glamour
3.notes:
You add your Wisdom modifier (minimum +1) to all Charisma checks.

You also gain proficiency in one: Deception, Performance, or Persuasion.

5.name: Extra Attack
5.notes: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

6.name: Roving
6.notes: Your Speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing Heavy armor. You also gain a Climb Speed and a Swim Speed equal to your walking Speed.

7.name: Beguiling Twist
7.notes:
You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed or Frightened condition.

Additionally, when you or a creature within 120 feet succeeds on a saving throw to avoid or end Charmed or Frightened, you may take a Reaction to force a different creature within 120 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, it is Charmed or Frightened (your choice) for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

traits.name: Elven Lineage
traits.notes: You are part of a lineage that grants you supernatural abilities. Choose a lineage from the Elven Lineages table. You gain the level 1 benefit of that lineage.When you reach character levels 3 and 5, you learn a higher-level spell, as shown on the table. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select the lineage).

traits.name: Fey Ancestry
traits.notes: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Charmed condition.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.notes: You have proficiency in the Insight, Perception, or Survival skill.

traits.name: Trance
traits.notes: You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep. You can finish a Long Rest in 4 hours if you spend those hours in a trancelike meditation, during which you retain consciousness

subrace.name: High Elf
subrace.notes: You know the Prestidigitation cantrip. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace that cantrip with a different cantrip from the Wizard spell list. Level2: - Detect Magic. Level3: - Misty Step

feats.notes: Initiative Proficiency. When you roll Initiative, you can add your Proficiency Bonus to the roll.Initiative Swap. Immediately after you roll Initiative, you can swap your Initiative with the Initiative of one willing ally in the same combat. You can't make this swap if you or the ally has the Incapacitated condition.
feats.name: Alert

feats.notes: Armor Training. You gain training with Medium armor.
feats.name: Moderately Armored
